name: Miasma
origin: unknown (built on Mini Shai-Hulud worm code publicly released by TeamPCP in May 2026)
description: Miasma is a self-replicating, credential-stealing worm that emerged in early June 2026 as the latest descendant of the Mini Shai-Hulud codebase TeamPCP released publicly in May 2026. The initial wave compromised 50+ npm packages — including at least 32 under the @redhat-cloud-services namespace (~80,000 weekly downloads) — via a 4.29MB obfuscated preinstall dropper, abusing GitHub Actions OIDC trusted publishing to forge SLSA provenance and push trojanized releases. A parallel Rust-based 'IronWorm' stealer variant uses an eBPF rootkit and Tor C2 to scrape developer secrets, while the 'Hades' wave hit PyPI with 37 malicious wheels across 19 packages using .pth startup-hook execution to deploy a Bun-based credential stealer targeting GitHub, npm, AWS, GCP, Azure, Anthropic, and CI/CD tokens. On June 5, 2026, the worm propagated using stolen contributor credentials to compromise 73 Microsoft GitHub repositories (Azure, Azure-Samples, Microsoft, MicrosoftDocs orgs), injecting configuration that triggers credential harvesting when the repo is opened in AI coding tools like Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, and VS Code. Attribution remains unclear — the campaign reuses TeamPCP's publicly released tooling but has not been definitively linked to the same operators.

ttps.technique_name: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies
ttps.notes: 50+ trojanized npm packages and 19 PyPI packages (37 malicious wheels) distributed via official registries
'Phantom Gyp' technique abuses 157-byte binding.gyp files to trigger code execution during npm install, bypassing pre/postinstall script monitoring
PyPI .pth startup-hook files auto-execute via Python's site module on interpreter startup, downloading the Bun runtime to run obfuscated payloads
Harvests GitHub, npm, PyPI, RubyGems, JFrog, CircleCI, Anthropic, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, Docker, Vault, and SSH credentials
Abuses GitHub Actions OIDC trusted publishing to mint short-lived npm tokens and push forged-provenance malicious releases
Worm replicates and spreads laterally across developer networks via SSH/SCP using stolen keys, then republishes trojanized packages
IronWorm Rust-based variant deploys an eBPF kernel rootkit to hide stealer activity from host monitoring
Stolen credentials exfiltrated to attacker-controlled GitHub repositories ('The Spreading Blight') and IronWorm exfiltrates over Tor C2

notable_techniques: Worm self-replicates by harvesting maintainer/contributor credentials and using them to publish further trojanized package versions
'Phantom Gyp' technique executes via binding.gyp during npm install, evading tools that only monitor pre/postinstall lifecycle scripts
Hades PyPI wave uses .pth startup hooks so malicious code runs on Python interpreter startup without the package ever being imported
Re-compromised the 'durabletask' package a second time after TeamPCP's original Mini Shai-Hulud infection the prior month
Compromised contributor credentials sat in infostealer logs for ~7 weeks (since April 13, 2026) before being weaponized for the GitHub org breach
Targets AI coding agents specifically — payload triggers when affected repos are opened in Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, or VS Code
GitHub disabled all 73 affected Microsoft repositories in an automated sweep within 105 seconds of detection
detection_opportunities: npm/pip installs triggering unexpected network connections to GitHub or Tor exit nodes during dependency installation
Presence of unexpected binding.gyp or *-setup.pth files in installed package trees, especially with embedded scripts/binaries
New attacker-controlled GitHub repositories created by developer or CI service accounts shortly after a suspicious package install
Anomalous OIDC token issuance and npm/PyPI publish events from CI/CD pipelines outside normal release windows
Unexpected outbound SSH/SCP connections from developer workstations to unfamiliar internal or external hosts
AI coding tool (Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, VS Code) opening a repo and immediately spawning shell processes or credential-access syscalls
Monitoring of Bun runtime downloads/execution on systems where Bun is not an expected dependency
